newsitem.title: USA: Calif. delays decision on PacEnt, Enova merger.
newsitem.headline: Calif. delays decision on PacEnt, Enova merger.

text.p: California Public Utilities Commission delayed until March 1998 a decision on the proposed merger of Pacific Enterprises and Enova Corp, the companies said Monday.
The new schedule was attributed to a delay in the state regulatory agency's ruling on a new rate proceeding for Southern California Gas Co, Pacific Enterprise's main subsidiary.
The companies had previously expected a final Commission ruling on the merger by the end of this year.

But a decision on a "performance-based ratemaking" scheme for SoCal Gas is not expected until July 16, which will push a final decision on the $5.2 billion merger to the first CPUC meeting next March, the companies said in a statement.
Officials at both Enova and Pacific Enterprises stressed the schedule is a procedural change, which is not reflective of the merger filing.

The companies announced plans last October to merge, combining SoCal Gas with Enova's San Diego Gas & Electric Co to form a combined gas and electric utility with an established Southern California customer base.
They had hoped to gain regulatory clearance for the deal in time for the January 1, 1998, opening of California's electricity market to full retail competition.
The merger is also subject to approval by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).
FERC last week delayed a ruling on the merger filing, but it could be addressed at the agency's next meeting later this month.
